title: d76f6931/A1: Route BitMatrix::matvec through popcnt SIMD dispatch
description:
## Current

`BitMatrix::matvec` at `crates/gf2-core/src/matrix.rs:962-988` computes parity per row with scalar `(row_word & x_word).count_ones() % 2`. The AVX2 popcount kernel (`LogicalFns::popcnt_fn`) already exists in `gf2-kernels-simd` but is never called from this path.

## Fix

Above a width threshold (initially: row width ≥ 8 u64 = 512 bits; tune empirically), reduce the row using `xor_fn` then call `popcnt_fn` once per row. Below threshold, keep the scalar path.

## PPC steps

V0 baseline (existing `matrix_vector` bench) → V3 SIMD via existing kernel dispatch → V0 measurement again to prove the gain.

## Per-kernel execution protocol (epic spec doc, all required)

1. Baseline saved (`ppc-v0-2026-04-25` already pinned by I1).
2. ASM artefact for the dispatched call site updated.
3. `perf stat -r 10` before/after recorded.
4. Proptest equivalence (I4 helper) for matvec on random matrices, all word-boundary widths.
5. ≥1.5× geomean over baseline at the design size class (matrices ≥ 512×512); else revert and try a different transform.
6. One commit `perf(jit:<this-short-id>): V3 — popcnt dispatch in BitMatrix::matvec`.
7. Lead-only gate transitions.

## Depends on

I1, I2, I3, I4.

## Success criteria

- [hard] Existing `matrix.rs` tests pass; new word-boundary `#[test]` for matvec passes.
- [hard] Proptest equivalence vs. scalar holds for all sizes 0..1024.
- [hard] Crossover threshold documented in code with the bench data point that justifies it.
- [aspirational] ≥1.5× at design size class.
